neuropeptide Y (a peptide hormone produced by the brain) stimulates growth hormone (a hormone secreted by the pituitary) secretion, and inhibits the release of luteinzing hormone (a hormone that stimulates ovulation and fertility), in sheep.

(i) NPY exerts an inhibitory effect on the secretion of LH, (ii) NPY stimulates secretion of GH during both its initiation and termination, and (iii) NPY may mediate the stimulatory effect of leptin on the secretion of GH.

NPY has been shown to be a potent stimulator of growth hormone release, and a potent inhibitor of luteinising hormone release.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NPY is a critical hypothalamic neuropeptide in regulating both growth and reproduction.
NPY is involved in mediating the effect of undernutrition on growth hormone (GH), luteinizing hormones (LH), and prolactin (PRL) secretion in ewes.
NPY may be a critical link between the nutritional status and neuro-endocrine regulation of growth and reproduction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the NPY system is important in regulating the secretion of LH and GH, but that the effect of NPY is dependent on the dose and duration of infusion, as well as on the nutritional state of the animal.
NPY can be a potent stimulator of GH secretion, but only at high doses.
NPY is a key player in regulating growth, metabolism and reproduction.
